details:
What It Does & How It Works:

We built THE SPACE HORIZON as a dual-platform space exploration system that connects an Astronaut Space Terminal with an Earth Mission Control center. Because crews in deep space cannot depend on constant internet, 80% of our platform works completely offline, while the remaining 20% connects online to stream live NASA MRO HiRISE and LRO imagery. Users can explore interactive 360-degree globes of Earth, the Moon, and Mars in four languages (Arabic, English, German, and French) with day and night modes. Crews can also extract exact coordinates, calculate surface distances, log field notes, and compare terrain elevation across different landing zones. Through our Analogue Base Lab, teams test closed-loop hydroponic farming, water-recycling irrigation, hybrid solar and Kilopower energy, and pressurized greenhouses on Earth first. When an emergency happens, astronauts send voice or text SOS alerts and research packets to Earth, while our vehicle-mounted Offline Edge-AI steps in with immediate rescue guidance in 0.00 seconds.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

By pairing accessible Earth environments with matching off-world terrain—Egypt’s White Desert with Jezero Crater, Wadi Rum with Gale Crater, Atacama with Arcadia Planitia, Antarctica’s McMurdo Dry Valleys with Shackleton Crater, Iceland’s lava tubes with Marius Hills, and Arizona’s volcanic field with South Pole–Aitken Basin—our platform helps researchers test survival systems safely before launching costly hardware into space. This lowers mission risks, prevents habitat failures, and ultimately protects human lives during long-duration lunar and Martian missions.

Tools & Technologies Used:

We developed the web applications using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, TypeScript, and React, alongside interactive 3D WebGL planetary rendering, Server-Sent Events (SSE) for real-time telemetry, and local browser caching to power our 80% offline core. To ground every feature in real science, we integrated official NASA Open APIs, Moon Trek (LRO WAC and LOLA topography), MRO HiRISE, Perseverance, Curiosity, and VIPER mission datasets, as well as Kilopower technical specifications. We also applied Delay-Tolerant Networking (DTN) concepts and the Web Speech API for hands-free voice SOS reporting across four languages.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:

Rather than building a static map or separate survival checklists, we brought planetary exploration, terrestrial analogue testing, and autonomous emergency response together into one connected workflow. Our platform pairs real geological twins side by side, simulates true light-speed communication delays (1.28 seconds for the Moon and 14 minutes 20 seconds one-way for Mars), and provides zero-latency Offline Edge-AI support. Throughout development, our team specifically accounted for 48-minute round-trip Mars signal blackouts, extreme lunar cold (-230°C in Permanently Shadowed Regions), toxic Martian perchlorate dust, reduced gravity (0.38g and 0.165g), and multilingual accessibility for international crews.
